film.contentHint: Search for a film or series and every field is filled. Or just type it yourself.
film.title: Film title
film.subtitle: Director
film.subtitleHint: Sits under the title, like the artist on an album poster.
film.showSubtitle: Show the director under the title
film.releaseDateLabelHint: What the release date is called on the poster. Leave empty for Premiere.
film.lengthLabelHint: What the runtime is called on the poster. Leave empty for Runtime.
film.lengthHint: Optional. Whole minutes; the poster prints e.g. “148 min”.
film.lengthInvalid: Enter the runtime in whole minutes, for example 148.
film.quoteHint: The line from the film that stuck with you. It looks best on the poster in quotation marks. Film quotes are usually protected by copyright, so without permission they are for a private poster only.
film.summaryHint: A film search puts the plot from Wikipedia here, shortened to a few sentences. Long paragraphs wrap on the poster by themselves. Wikipedia text is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0; for a published or sold poster, the terms of use apply.
film.previewEmptyHint: Set a title and the cast, and the preview shows up here.
film.qrHint: Where the poster's QR code points. The film's Wikipedia article by default; clear it to remove the QR code.

filmSearch.placeholder: Search for a film or series …
filmSearch.title: Search films
filmSearch.description: Films and series from Wikidata. Director, cast and runtime come from there, the summary from Wikipedia.
filmSearch.note: The search uses Wikidata and Wikipedia and only takes text from them: title, director, cast and plot. It never loads images. More in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.
filmSearch.sources_wikipedia: Title, dates, cast, crew and awards: <wikidata>Wikidata</wikidata> (CC0). Plot: <wikipedia>Wikipedia, “{{title}}”</wikipedia>, <license>CC BY-SA 4.0</license>.
filmSearch.sources_none: Title, dates, cast, crew and awards: <wikidata>Wikidata</wikidata> (CC0). No plot was found.
filmSearch.replaceHint: Both options refill title, director, date, runtime, info, cast, awards and summary. Whatever you changed there yourself is gone afterwards.
